Rights and removal

Other people’s work
stays theirs.

This catalogue studies and describes visual design. It does not own, license, or endorse the works it references.

This is a general notice. Each reference page records its own source, rights tier, and license when known. This page will become more specific as the catalogue grows.

Ownership

Websites, products, printed works, objects, images, typefaces, names, and trademarks shown or described here belong to their owners. A reference in this catalogue does not mean that the owner is affiliated with it, approves of it, or agrees with its notes. Style names and placements are interpretations by the catalogue unless a page says otherwise.

Why images appear here

Screenshots and images identify the work under discussion and support commentary, research, and teaching about design. Each one is credited, dated, and linked to its source where a source exists. Screenshots are kept at a modest size. The catalogue grants no license to any third-party material. To use a work, get permission from its owner or rely on the license the owner gives.

Rights tiers

Tier A
The image has an open license or public-domain statement, and the work shown is itself in the public domain in the United States and in its country of origin, or is not protected by copyright. Example: a CC0 museum photograph of a 1923 poster whose designer died in 1948. The image is stored here with its license.
Tier C
A third-party work that may be in copyright, captured or copied for commentary. The image is stored with credit and a link to its source. No license is claimed.
Tier D
Link and metadata only. No image is stored, because the source’s terms do not allow it or the rights are unclear.

A license recorded as unverified means that nobody has confirmed the rights. Treat such material as all rights reserved.

Measurements and tokens

Measured values such as colors, sizes, and font names describe what a source showed on the capture date. Design tokens and implementations in this catalogue are new work that describes a general style. They do not copy any single source. The tokens are MIT licensed, as the next section explains. Fonts named in tokens keep their own licenses.

Accuracy

Websites and products change, and interpretations can be wrong. Every reference has a review date. Placements marked as agent-proposed have not been reviewed by a person.

License for the catalogue’s code and tokens

The catalogue’s original code and design tokens are free to reuse under the MIT License, copyright 2026 Switchback Solutions LLC. You can copy, change, and ship them in any project, including commercial projects. Keep the copyright notice and the license text with copies of substantial portions. The generated token files carry a short notice that points to this section.

What the MIT License covers

  • Design tokens: data/tokens/ and everything in implementations/. That includes tokens.json, tokens.css, tailwind.css, shadcn.css, registry-item.json, DESIGN.md, and the specimen page and stylesheet, with the style descriptions and rules that those files contain.
  • Specimens: the stylesheets in data/specimens/ and the fictional sample content in content/specimen.html.
  • Code: tools/, assets/hub.css, package.json, and wrangler.jsonc.
  • Schemas and templates: data/schema/ and templates/.
  • Procedures: skills/ and .claude/skills/.

What it does not cover: third-party material

The catalogue cannot license work that it does not own. These things keep their owners’ rights and licenses, wherever they appear in the repository or on the site:

  • Reference images and screenshots in assets/references/, and the works that they show. Each reference page records its own license. A Tier C image has no license for reuse.
  • Typefaces. Tokens name fonts such as Futura, but the catalogue includes no font files. Get each font under its own license.
  • Names, trademarks, and logos of people, companies, products, and works.
  • Titles, quotations, credits, and source metadata copied from a source, such as a museum record. They keep the source’s terms.
  • Measurements of third-party websites and images in data/measurements/. They record what a source showed. They grant no rights in that source.

If a covered file contains third-party material, that material keeps its own license. A license recorded on a reference page applies to that reference, not this section.

The catalogue’s own text and data

The MIT License does not yet cover the catalogue’s original prose and catalogue data: the style and reference records in data/styles/ and data/references/, the prose pages in content/, the specimen screenshots in assets/specimens/, and the generated pages, api/, llms.txt, and board-data.js. A license for them has not been chosen. You need no license to read them, link to them, or let an agent read api/ to choose a style. For other reuse, ask first. A future license for this text and data will cover only the catalogue’s own words and structure, not the third-party material that they describe.

Removal requests

If you own a work referenced here and want it corrected, credited differently, or removed, email hello@switchbacksolutions.net. Name the page and the work. The catalogue will remove a stored image promptly on a reasonable request and will keep a record of the change.
